aboutAuthor: Mahendra Ramsinghani is a Michigan-based investor and author of University of Michigan's Venture Capital course. He synthesizes fifty-plus GPs and LPs into the lifecycle of raising, investing, governing, and exiting a venture fund.

points.heading: Cash and carry is fund economics
points.body: 2 and 20 waterfall with hurdle and fees means median TVPI yields little carry; entry price and vintage determine GP wealth more than picking stories.

points.heading: Career is references not pedigree
points.body: LPs diligence character via back-channel and decline etiquette because enemies accumulate quickly; 24-hour responsiveness and gracious passes preserve optionality over decades.

points.heading: Raise by warehousing and sequencing
points.body: Three to five personal warehouse deals plus FOF first creates credibility cascade of 100 meetings to two closes over nine months.

points.heading: Sourcing is system, diligence is canvas
points.body: Forty percent outbound via research triggers and four-week cheat sheet with customer calls ensures pipeline quality before diligence perfection.

points.heading: Terms set governance, board creates value
points.body: 1x non-participating, caps, and anti-dilution protect; boards that let founders talk seventy percent add value via customers and hires not directives.

points.heading: Exits serve the power law
points.body: One 50x winner returns the fund; acquisitions with earnouts, IPO with greenshoe, and secondaries must let that winner run rather than sell too early.

insights: 2 and 20 waterfall illustration where fees consume eighteen percent before a single exit, making top-quartile TVPI of 2.8 the real carry threshold.
Fund-of-funds trust cascade where a three million anchor from a Minneapolis FOF unlocked two pensions and twenty-five million close.
Continuation fund diagram where LPs choose to roll or redeem, creating liquidity without forced M&A when IPO window shut.
conclusion: The Business of Venture Capital maps the full lifecycle from carry math to continuation funds, showing that structure, sourcing system, and governance discipline let a ten-year illiquid carry business compound relationships into outlier returns.
